Every morning, the lighthouse keeper climbed the stairs and opened the window at the top, though the lamp had been automated for years.

He said the room needed fresh air. The villagers knew better: he was listening for the bell on his daughter’s boat.

She had painted the bell blue when she was seven and insisted it sounded different afterward. He had laughed, but he listened anyway, through summers and storms, through the years when she sailed farther than he could see.

One morning, he heard it ring twice.

By the time he reached the harbor, she was tying up beside the pier. She looked tired and happy, and her boat needed paint.

“The bell still sounds blue,” he told her.

“I know,” she said. “That’s how I found my way home.”
